name: security-ios-oauth-callback-routing-review
intent: iOS OAuth callback routing and authorization-transaction binding
artifacts: URL scheme/universal-link configuration, authentication session API, PKCE/state storage and callback consumer.
trace: Trace OS-delivered callback fields into the exact pending client/account transaction and token exchange, distinguishing routing from session binding.
experiment: Use owned client/issuer fixtures and two local login transactions; compare intended callback with a swapped transaction or wrong callback origin.
disproof: A custom scheme is not automatically exploitable if PKCE/transaction validation stops code use; an intercepted route alone does not prove token theft.
repair: Bind routing and pending authorization state, preserving approved browser-to-app and cross-device behavior.
branch_decisions: Match the registered callback scheme/universal link, state and PKCE to the initiating app transaction. ASWebAuthenticationSession handling can differ from a general deep-link route. An unrelated app registering the same scheme does not prove code redemption; the code, verifier and session must reach an unauthorized consumer in the supplied local model.
operational_method: Choose the actual callback mechanism, such as ASWebAuthenticationSession matching versus a general custom-scheme/universal-link handler. Retain the initiating session/transaction, expected callback, state/PKCE context and cancellation/retry mapping. Compare two concurrent owned sign-ins and a callback arriving after cancellation. A callback reaching the app does not prove the wrong local transaction redeemed the code; bind the final session creation result.
